hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Every character added increases total value by its count among identical characters before it.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Total cost depends solely on multiset of character frequencies, so greedily pick characters with smallest current frequency.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Tally fixed character counts. For each question mark, assign the character with smallest frequency (tiebreak alphabetically). Sort the replacements alphabetically and insert into question mark spots.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimizeStringValue(self, s: str) -> str:
        import heapq
        from collections import Counter
        cnt = Counter(c for c in s if c != '?')
        heap = [(cnt[chr(ord('a') + i)], chr(ord('a') + i)) for i in range(26)]
        heapq.heapify(heap)
        q_count = s.count('?')
        picks = []
        for _ in range(q_count):
            c_freq, ch = heapq.heappop(heap)
            picks.append(ch)
            heapq.heappush(heap, (c_freq + 1, ch))
        picks.sort()
        res = list(s)
        p_idx = 0
        for i in range(len(res)):
            if res[i] == '?':
                res[i] = picks[p_idx]
                p_idx += 1
        return ''.join(res)
```

complexity.notes: Greedy frequency balancing with min-heap and sorting chosen replacements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all 26^q replacement assignments is exponential.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary list for modified string.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Notice that placement order within ? positions should be sorted alphabetically to minimize string lexicographically.
